exposure: American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) score at primary intervention
availability of ventilation or parenteral nutrition
use of a peripherally inserted central catheter
use of a percutaneous central line
cohort: The cohort comprised 3849 patients younger than 16 years, presenting for the first time with one of seven common gastrointestinal congenital anomalies, recruited from 264 hospitals across 74 low-income, middle-income, and high-income countries.
finding: Mortality for gastrointestinal congenital anomalies was significantly higher in low-income (39.8%) and middle-income (20.4%) countries compared to high-income countries (5.6%), with various clinical and resource-related factors further associated with mortality.
country: 74 countries (across low-income, middle-income, and high-income classifications)
followup_time: 30 days after primary intervention or 30 days after admission
birth_weight: median bodyweight at presentation was 2.8 kg (IQR 2.3-3.3)
